title: What a prophet is
hookLine: a prophet is less a fortune-teller than one who speaks to the present on God's behalf

cards: Crystal ball. Tarot cards. A man on a street corner with a sign about the end of the world.
Say the word prophet in ordinary English and that's often what comes up: someone who tells the future.
The Hebrew Bible has a section called the Prophets, and today its second half begins: the books named for the prophets, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel and the shorter books that follow them.
First, what does the Bible mean by the word?

teach.h: A PROPHET WAS ONCE CALLED A SEER.
teach.b: The Hebrew word is navi, and the Bible itself notices that words change. In the book of Samuel there's a little note to the reader: "he that is now called a prophet was beforetime called a seer." So what does a navi do?
Look at the ones already met.

Nathan walks into King David's palace, tells him a story about a rich man who stole a poor man's lamb, and when David is furious, says: "Thou art the man." That's not a forecast. That's the present, named out loud.
Elijah stands on Mount Carmel and asks how long the people will waver between two opinions. Huldah tells a king what the book in his hands means for him today.

teach.h: A WARNING WITH A DOOR LEFT OPEN.
teach.b: A navi does sometimes speak about what's coming, but often it's a warning with a door left open: if you change, this need not happen. Jonah announces that Nineveh will be overthrown. The city repents, and it isn't.
The prophecy worked by not coming true. And prophets were often not who you'd pick. Amos says, in effect: I wasn't a prophet or a prophet's son.

teach.h: A HERDSMAN, TAKEN FROM THE FLOCK.
teach.b: I was a herdsman, I tended sycamore figs, and God took me from following the flock. A navi speaks to now, on God's behalf, usually to people who would rather not hear it, and often at real cost.
That's the voice in Isaiah, Jeremiah and Ezekiel: less about predicting tomorrow, more about what is happening today, and what God asks of it.

how: In Jewish practice, passages from the Prophets are read in the synagogue after the Torah reading on Shabbat and holidays; this reading is called the haftarah.

a prophet, who speaks to the present for God

games.q: you're Nathan. the king has done something terrible and doesn't see it. how do you tell him?
o: announce it publicly in the city gate.
tell him a story, then say: thou art the man.
games.why: Nathan tells David about a rich man who took a poor man's lamb, and when David is angry, says: thou art the man.

practice: Think of something true that someone near you needs to hear, maybe even yourself, and that you've been avoiding.
Shape it the way Nathan did, not as an attack but as something they can actually take in, with a first sentence that begins with care. If you pray, you can ask for kind words.

wordCard.voice: Navi. The Hebrew word for a prophet: one who speaks to the present on God's behalf, more than one who predicts the future. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: a prophet; the second section of the Hebrew Bible is called Nevi'im, the Prophets.

carryVoice: Your line: a prophet speaks to now. Less crystal ball, more door left open. Until tomorrow.
